chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani the judge informed me, saying: Ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Hamzah ibn al-Abbas al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Nasr ibn Hajib narrated to us, saying: Warqa ibn Umar, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed God, the Mighty and Exalted, despises the eloquent in bad speech, the coarse, the beggar, and the persistent requester.

key_terms.سَائِل: Beggar or one who asks for things
key_terms.فَاحِش: One who is eloquent in bad speech or speaks foully
key_terms.مُلْحِف: One who persists in asking or is persistent in requests

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics despised by God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to outline the moral vices that incur divine displeasure, emphasizing the interplay between speech and action. The term 'al-mulhaf' specifically denotes one who persists in asking, often implying a lack of dignity or excessive dependence, which aligns with the Shia ethical focus on self-respect and moderation. This teaching serves as a practical guide for cultivating refined character (akhlaq) by avoiding both verbal coarseness and behavioral excess.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-147 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated that Ibn Sa’ed quoted Hamzih ibn al-Abbas al-Marvazy, on the authority of Yahya ibn Nasr ibn Hajib, on the authority of Varqa ibn Umar, on the authority of al-A’amash, on the authority of Abi Salih, on the authority of Abi Hurayrih that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “The Honorable the Exalted God despises one who swears, is corrupt, begs or makes persistent requests.”
